title: Borrow-forward protocol for reserved-capacity intra-cycle shortfalls and reconciliation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Introduce a borrow-forward protocol that permits controlled, auditable borrowing of reserved quota from a tenant's upcoming billing cycle to cover intra-cycle consumption spikes. This is targeted at reserved GPU pools and aims to reduce application errors and throttles for high-value customers while preserving predictable billing and preventing unbounded overdraft. The system applies eligibility rules, soft caps, and automated reconciliation with optional credits or post-payment adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Eligible reserved tenants can borrow up to a configured percentage (default 15%) of next-cycle allocation when current-cycle usage exceeds threshold
Borrowed usage is tracked on ledger entries and visible in Console token-level billing UI within 5 minutes
Reconciliation job runs post-cycle and either applies credits, produces invoices, or rolls back borrow entries according to policy
No impact to existing non-reserved tenants or hosted API quotas
Automated telemetry alerts trigger when borrowed volume exceeds 20% of pool capacity or when net reconciliation delta > 5% for a tenant
decisions: Use borrow windows aligned to tenant timezone anchor to avoid cross-day surprises
Implement borrow cap as percent of next-cycle reserved allocation rather than fixed tokens to support different contract sizes
Ledger model: append-only borrow and repay entries with transaction IDs; avoid modifying historical committed usage records
Reconciliation modes: auto-invoice (default) or apply account credit when tenant has credit balance; allow manual admin override via Console
design_tradeoffs: Pros: reduces incidence of immediate throttles for bursty workloads, better UX for Reserved customers; enables smoother traffic shifting across month boundary
Cons: increases complexity in billing reconciliation, edge cases with tenant churn mid-cycle, potential cashflow/credit exposure for Redwood
Tradeoff: prefer conservative default cap (15%) and require explicit opt-in for higher caps to limit exposure
migration_notes: DB: add borrow_ledger table (append-only) with columns: id, tenant_id, cycle_start, borrow_tokens, created_at, resolved_at, resolution_type, linked_invoice_id
Backfill: existing reserved tenants start with zero borrowed balance. Historical usage not migrated.
Feature flag: borrow_forward_enabled per-tenant to allow staged rollout and immediate rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable on staging for 3 enterprise tenants and run synthetic burst tests
Phase 2 (pilot): opt-in for 10 high-usage reserved customers for 2 billing cycles
Phase 3 (ramp): enable conservative default (15%) for all reserved tenants; monitor 2 cycles before raising cap
Rollback: toggle borrow_forward_enabled off and run reconciliation to avoid leaving unaccounted borrowed balances
implementation_notes: Quota evaluation path: when request would exceed current_cycle_remaining, check borrow eligibility and reserve borrowed_tokens atomically with existing lease path
Token reservation must be idempotent across retries and survive leader failover — use lease IDs tied to request GUIDs
Billing pipeline: augment usage aggregator to emit borrow markers so invoicing service can separate borrowed vs earned usage
Edge-case: tenant downgrade mid-cycle triggers immediate reconciliation and optional invoice for borrowed portion
tasks: Schema migration and borrow_ledger implementation (ENG backend)
Modify quota-check service to consult borrow-cap and create borrow ledger entry atomically
Expose borrow balance and history in Console usage page
Add reconciliation worker that finalizes borrows at cycle boundary and emits Billing adjustments
Add unit/integration tests for idempotency and failover scenarios
Create docs and update billing FAQ + Sales playbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: tenants churn between borrow and reconciliation -> Mitigation: require tenant contract check and prohibit borrowing if contract termination is scheduled
Risk: unexpected high borrowed volume creates cashflow risk -> Mitigation: conservative default cap, realtime alerts and manual pause capability
Risk: accounting divergence -> Mitigation: append-only ledger and nightly audit job that reconciles aggregator and ledger
